analysis.summary: In Q1 FY27, Krishana Phoschem Limited reported revenue from operations of ₹532 crore, representing a 35% year-on-year growth, while quarterly PAT rose 54% to ₹47 crore. The company operated its SSP unit at 121% capacity utilization and its NPK-DAP unit at 43% capacity utilization during the quarter. Management expects to achieve a quarterly turnover of more than ₹500 crore over the remaining three quarters of FY27 as raw material supply constraints ease. Additionally, the company completed a 5-for-1 stock split, subdividing the face value of its equity shares from ₹10 to ₹2 per share. Krishana Phoschem Limited reported its Q1 FY27 results, achieving revenue from operations of ₹532.3 crore (up 34.58% YoY) and Profit After Tax of ₹47.06 crore (up 53.88% YoY).

guidance.claim: The company expects to achieve revenue growth of 30% to 35% for the year.
guidance.quote: We hope that we will be able to achieve our target for this year, which comes to around 25% of last year's revenue. So, your figure of 30%–35%, we can say that we will be able to achieve it.

guidance.claim: Management expects quarterly revenue to exceed ₹500 crore for the remaining quarters of FY27.
guidance.quote: We expect to achieve a quarterly turnover of more than ₹500 crore over the remaining three quarters of FY27, supported by improved capacity utilization and production.

guidance.claim: Management expressed confidence in maintaining operational and financial momentum through the remainder of FY27.
guidance.quote: We are confident of building on this momentum through the remainder of FY27, as we continue strengthening India's agri-future for our farmers, partners, & shareholders

guidance.claim: The company expects to deliver over 40% growth across key parameters during FY27.
guidance.quote: Accordingly, we expect to deliver growth of over 40% across key parameters during the current year.

guidance.claim: Krishana Phoschem expects a top-line revenue increase of around Rs. 500 crore from the newly expanded capacity.
guidance.quote: So, you expect an increase of around Rs. 500 crore more, Rs. 2,900 to Rs. 3,000.

guidance.claim: The company expects to import around 150,000 metric tons of material translating into approximately Rs. 1,000 crore of revenue in FY27.
guidance.quote: For FY27, based on market demand, we expect to import around 150,000 metric tons of material, which would translate into approximately Rs.1,000 crore of revenue.

guidance.claim: Krishana Phoschem expects manufacturing growth to be in the range of 25% in FY27.
guidance.quote: And based on the capacity utilization on a reasonable level, the growth in the manufacturing will be in the range of 25%.

demand_outlook.claim: National Kharif sowing declined by 22.7% year-on-year to 182.7 lakh hectares by the end of June due to rainfall deficit.
demand_outlook.quote: By the end of June, cumulative rainfall was nearly 40% below normal, resulting in national Kharif sowing declining by 22.7% year-on-year to 182.7 lakh hectares, compared to 236.5 lakh hectares during the corresponding period last year.

demand_outlook.claim: Monsoon revival in early July led to accelerated fertilizer offtake across key markets.
demand_outlook.quote: However, rainfall improved materially during early July, resulting in a rapid recovery in sowing progress, improved farmer sentiment, and accelerated fertilizer offtake across several key markets for the remainder of the Kharif season.

demand_outlook.claim: During April-May 2026, industry-wide fertilizer production dropped by 28% year-on-year while SSP production fell 7%.
demand_outlook.quote: During the April-May 2026 period, industry-wide production declined by 28% year-on-year, while SSP production dropped by around 7% year-on-year.

demand_outlook.claim: Domestic fertilizer manufacturers are unlikely to face demand pressure as nearly 40% of phosphatic fertilizers are imported.
demand_outlook.quote: From our perspective, domestic manufacturers are unlikely to face demand pressure. Even hypothetically, if demand were to soften, it is important to note that nearly 40% of phosphatic fertilizers are imported.

demand_outlook.claim: Fertilizer demand is expected to remain stable supported by higher water levels in major reservoirs, rivers, and borewells.
demand_outlook.quote: Also, water levels in major reservoirs, rivers, and borewells are higher compared to earlier periods in the country. Therefore, we do not expect any stress on the agriculture sector, and consequently, fertilizer demand is expected to remain stable.

capex_expansion.claim: The company is evaluating capacity expansion opportunities that are not yet approved by the Board.
capex_expansion.quote: We are currently evaluating certain capacity expansion opportunities.

capex_expansion.claim: The third-party green ammonia capacity under agreement is scheduled to start in FY29.
capex_expansion.quote: And this capacity will start in FY29 after 2 years.

capex_expansion.claim: Krishana Phoschem expanded its capacities at Meghnagar to 165,000 MTPA for NPK/DAP and 99,000 MTPA for Sulphuric Acid.
capex_expansion.quote: Our expanded capacities at Meghnagar — NPK/DAP at 165,000 MTPA and Sulphuric Acid at 99,000 MTPA — are now contributing progressively to our performance.

capex_expansion.claim: The company enhanced its NPK/DAP capacity by 50% to 495,000 MTPA, taking total phosphatic fertilizer capacity to 615,000 MTPA.
capex_expansion.quote: NPK/DAP capacity enhanced by 50% to 495,000 MTPA and existing SSP capacity at 120,000 MTPA, taking total phosphatic fertilizer capacity to 615,000 MTPA

capex_expansion.claim: Krishana Phoschem strengthened its backward integration with a sulphuric acid capacity of 99,000 MTPA.
capex_expansion.quote: Backward integration strengthened with sulphuric acid capacity of 99,000 MTPA

capex_expansion.claim: The company entered into a 10-year Green Ammonia Sale Agreement for 70,000 MTPA under India's National Green Hydrogen Mission.
capex_expansion.quote: As part of our long-term sustainability strategy, Krishana Phoschem has entered into a 10-year Green Ammonia Sale Agreement (GASA) under India’s National Green Hydrogen Mission for 70,000 MTPA.

margins_costs.claim: Quarterly EBITDA grew 36% year-on-year to ₹89 crore.
margins_costs.quote: Quarterly EBITDA stood at ₹ 89 crore, reflecting a 36% year-on-year growth, supported by disciplined cost management, despite volatility in raw material prices.

margins_costs.claim: EBITDA margin is approximately 7% to 8% for trading and around 16% for manufacturing.
margins_costs.quote: The EBITDA margin is approximately 7%–8% for trading and around 16% for manufacturing.

margins_costs.claim: The company passed on approximately 25% to 30% of raw material input cost increases.
margins_costs.quote: Overall, we have been able to pass on ~ 25%–30% of the increase in input costs.

margins_costs.claim: Inventory carried forward at lower costs from the previous quarter contributed to higher EBITDA margins.
margins_costs.quote: Yes, the inventory carried forward from the previous quarter at lower costs did contribute to the higher EBITDA margins.

margins_costs.claim: Quarterly Profit After Tax grew 53.88% YoY to ₹47.06 crore driven by operating efficiency and cost control.
margins_costs.quote: Quaterly Profit After Tax grew 53.88% YoY to ₹47.06 crore, reflecting improved operating efficiency and disciplined cost control.

margins_costs.claim: EBITDA margins were not under pressure during Q4 FY26 due to adequate inventory levels maintained throughout the year.
margins_costs.quote: Input costs increased towards the latter part of Q4. However, we maintain adequate inventory levels throughout the year. Therefore, EBITDA margins were not under pressure during Q4.

margins_costs.claim: Manufacturing EBITDA per ton was in the range of Rs. 5,500 per ton in FY26.
margins_costs.quote: It was in the range of Rs.5,500 per ton.

margins_costs.claim: Sulphur prices are fluctuating in the range of Rs. 55,000 to Rs. 70,000 per ton depending on supplier and purchasing terms.
margins_costs.quote: The prices are changing and prices are in the range of around Rs.55,000 to Rs.70,000 per ton, depending on the supplier and what time we are buying and what are the payment terms.

margins_costs.claim: Overall EBITDA margin moderated from 13.54% in FY25 to 12.34% in FY26 due to lower margins on trading turnover.
margins_costs.quote: Our overall EBITDA margin, which was 13.54% has come down to 12.34%.

orders_capacity.claim: Total fertilizer production reached 89,747 metric tonnes in Q1 FY27.
orders_capacity.quote: Achieved fertilizer production of 89,747 metric tonnes, showcasing our consistent operational efficiency.

orders_capacity.claim: Capacity utilization was 43% for the NPK-DAP unit and 121% for the SSP unit during Q1 FY27.
orders_capacity.quote: 43% capacity utilization of NPK-DAP unit and 121% capacity utilization of SSP unit, which was beyond the core.

orders_capacity.claim: Total NPK-DAP capacity reached 495,000 MT after adding 165,000 MT of new capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: Our existing NPK-DAP capacity is 330,000 MT, and we have added another 165,000 MT, taking the total capacity to 495,000 MT.

orders_capacity.claim: Sales volumes were 53,500 MT for NPK-DAP, 36,300 MT for SSP, and 21,000 MT for trading in Q1 FY27.
orders_capacity.quote: For NPK-DAP, it was 53,500 MT, for SSP 36,300 MT

orders_capacity.claim: The company has a total installed fertilizer capacity of 6.15 Lakh MTPA.
The company achieved total fertilizer production of 397,263 MT for FY26.
orders_capacity.quote: Achieved total production of 397,263 MT, supported by High demand across markets

orders_capacity.claim: In FY26, manufacturing volumes were approximately 383,000 metric tons and trading volumes were around 93,000 metric tons.
orders_capacity.quote: Trading volumes were approximately 93,000 metric tons, while manufacturing volumes were around 383,000 metric tons.

orders_capacity.claim: Current utilization of the company's 200,000-ton rock phosphate beneficiation capacity is in the range of 50% to 75%.
orders_capacity.quote: The beneficiation capacity is around 200,000 tons, and current utilization is in the range of 50% to 75%.

capital_allocation.claim: The company executed a 5-for-1 stock split reducing face value from ₹10 to ₹2 per share.
capital_allocation.quote: Recently, the company successfully executed a 5-for-1 stock split, subdividing the face value of our equity shares from ₹ 10 per share to ₹ 2 per share.

capital_allocation.claim: Depreciation increased to ₹13 crore and finance costs rose to ₹20 crore following capacity commissioning.
capital_allocation.quote: Depreciation increased from around ₹8.7 crore to ₹13 crore, while finance costs increased from around ₹13 crore to ₹20 crore.

capital_allocation.claim: Disciplined capital allocation is one of Krishana Phoschem's five core strategic pillars.
capital_allocation.quote: Our strategic blueprint rests on five core pillars: backward integration, capacity expansion, product diversification, disciplined capital allocation and deep farmer connect.

capital_allocation.claim: Capacity expansion was funded through internal accruals and term loans.
capital_allocation.quote: This expansion has been funded through a prudent mix of internal accruals and term loans, reflecting disciplined capital allocation.

capital_allocation.claim: The company's effective interest cost across borrowing facilities ranges between 6% and 7.5%.
capital_allocation.quote: Overall, the effective interest cost is in the range of 6% to 7.5%.

risks_headwinds.claim: Geopolitical tensions in West Asia around the Strait of Hormuz created supply chain uncertainties and raised freight costs.
risks_headwinds.quote: Geopolitical tensions in West Asia, particularly surrounding critical shipping lanes through the Strait of Hormuz, introduced considerable uncertainty across global industry, global fertilizer supply chains during the quarter.

risks_headwinds.claim: Raw material availability was the primary operational challenge during Q1 FY27.
risks_headwinds.quote: The primary challenge during the first quarter was the availability of raw materials.

risks_headwinds.claim: Sulphur prices increased from ₹65,000–₹70,000 per tonne in April to nearly ₹1 lakh per tonne in June and July.
risks_headwinds.quote: Sulphur prices have risen from around ₹65,000–₹70,000 per tonne in April to almost ₹1 lakh per tonne in June and July.

risks_headwinds.claim: Input cost volatility and global supply uncertainties remain key monitorable factors for the industry.
risks_headwinds.quote: On the other hand, input cost volatility and global supply uncertainties remain key monitorable.

risks_headwinds.claim: The company expects margin pressure in Q1 FY27 before margins stabilize later in the year as cost increases get passed on.
risks_headwinds.quote: While there may be some margin pressure in the first quarter, we expect margins to stabilize in the later part of the year as cost increases are passed on.
